# AI Support for Image-Guided Therapy (IGT) Procedures

## Current Challenges AI Can Address

Image-guided procedures—particularly cardiac interventions—face several persistent challenges:
- Radiation exposure (fluoroscopy time averaging roughly 15-45 minutes per complex ablation procedure)
- Procedural variability between operators (success rates can vary by approximately 10-20% between high-volume and low-volume centers)
- Real-time decision-making under time pressure
- Difficulty integrating multiple imaging modalities (echo, CT, MRI, fluoroscopy) simultaneously

## Key AI Approaches for IGT

### 1. **Real-Time Image Segmentation and Registration**
- Deep learning models (typically U-Net or nnU-Net architectures) can segment cardiac chambers in under 1-2 seconds per frame, compared to manual segmentation taking 5-10 minutes
- Automated fusion of pre-procedural CT/MRI with live fluoroscopy or intracardiac echo, reducing registration errors from roughly 3-5mm (manual) to under 1-2mm

### 2. **Motion Compensation and Tracking**
- AI-based catheter tip tracking can achieve accuracy within approximately 0.5-1.5mm
- Respiratory and cardiac motion compensation algorithms can reduce image blur/artifact by an estimated 40-60%

### 3. **Predictive Analytics for Procedural Guidance**
- Machine learning models predicting optimal ablation lesion parameters (contact force typically targeting 10-20 grams, ablation duration of roughly 20-40 seconds per lesion)
- Risk stratification models flagging complications with reported AUC values of approximately 0.80-0.90 in retrospective studies

### 4. **Radiation Dose Reduction**
- AI-enhanced image reconstruction from low-dose fluoroscopy can reduce radiation exposure by an estimated 30-50% while maintaining diagnostic image quality
- Some systems report reducing fluoroscopy time by roughly 20-35% through improved visualization

---

## Specific Applications in Cardiac Treatment

### **Atrial Fibrillation (AFib) Ablation**
- AI algorithms analyze electroanatomical mapping data to identify arrhythmogenic substrate, with some studies showing improved first-pass isolation rates from baseline ~70% to approximately 85-90%
- Automated detection of pulmonary vein anatomy variants (present in roughly 20-30% of patients) reduces procedural planning time by an estimated 15-25 minutes

### **Structural Heart Disease (TAVR/TAVI)**
- AI-based annulus sizing algorithms improve valve size selection accuracy, potentially reducing paravalvular leak incidence (historically occurring in approximately 10-15% of cases) to below 5%
- Automated CT analysis for calcium scoring and access route assessment can cut planning time from roughly 30-45 minutes to under
